# Experimental Classroom Games {.unnumbered}

These activities connect strategic reasoning with observed play. Each game
provides rules, a normal-form model, a mathematical analysis, and a discussion
of the classroom results. The collection will grow as further games are
played in the course.

The distinction between a model and its interpretation is central: an
equilibrium describes mutually consistent best responses, while actual
choices also depend on expectations, experience, and communication. Classroom
records let us examine this distinction without treating a small group as a
controlled study of human behaviour.

- [Two Thirds of the Average](two-thirds-of-average.qmd): a guessing game
  about others' choices and reasoning, with a continuous-distance payoff,
  a complete best-response and dominance analysis, and results from six
  players over three rounds.
